requirement:
> `Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes
> separately.`
rationale:
structural: The text of `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.mcp.description` only fixes the description string of the `search_text` tool: "Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes separately." It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface. An implementation could build the tool definition another way and still advertise the same description. Examples are a constant, a different builder, or a different serialization path. Those would meet the text just as well. So the clause is observable behavior, and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied root, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]`, does emit a `SEARCH_TEXT` definition. Its description is exactly the required string. This matches the text, but the match is not a structural requirement. No further roots or corrections are needed.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.mcp.description` has one observable obligation. The published `search_text` tool description must be exactly: "Find regular-expression matches in available files, optionally within a file or directory. Read selected nodes separately."

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` covers it. The test builds `ProjectSources` and reads the session's tool definitions. It finds the `search_text` definition by name and uses `assert_eq!` to compare its `description` with that exact string. The string matches the requirement text word for word, so any wording change, omission or extra text would fail the test.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_pages_return_every_original_match_in_order]` also carries a `{test}` reference to this requirement. It checks the parameter schema and paging, which the description requirement does not cover. It adds nothing needed here and does no harm.

I found no gaps.
